config.title: Invert Binary Tree

intro.title: Invert Binary Tree
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a function that inverts a binary tree, flipping it horizontally so that each left child becomes a right child and vice versa. You'll learn the core concept of tree traversal, specifically using recursion to visit and swap nodes. The main technologies involved are JavaScript functions, recursion, and basic tree node structures. This exercise will help you understand how to manipulate tree data structures and think recursively, which are fundamental skills in algorithm design.
intro.usecase: Inverting a binary tree is a core pattern for manipulating hierarchical data structures, which appear in many real-world UI components. For example, you might use this algorithm to flip a nested navigation menu, reverse the order of a collapsible file explorer, or mirror a tree-view component in a dashboard. Understanding this concept helps developers efficiently reorganize or transform any tree-like data, such as comment threads, organizational charts, or settings panels, by recursively swapping child nodes.

objectives: Implement a recursive function to invert a binary tree
Apply tree traversal techniques to manipulate node connections
Construct a solution that swaps left and right child nodes at each level
Initialize and test the inversion algorithm with sample binary trees
Manipulate tree structure by reassigning node references
Integrate base cases to handle empty trees or leaf nodes
Control the recursion flow to traverse all nodes systematically

content.body: Have you ever looked at a tree and wondered what it would look like upside down? In this lesson, we'll flip a binary tree by swapping its left and right branches at every node. You'll learn how to systematically explore and transform tree structures.
content.title: Welcome

content.body:
• Apply tree traversal to visit every node
• Implement a function that swaps left and right children
• Explain why we need to handle empty trees as a base case
• Recognize the pattern of exploring branches from the root
content.title: What you'll learn

content.body: Imagine a small tree with root value 4, left child 2, and right child 7. If you swap the left and right branches at the root, what becomes the new left child?
content.title: Try it
content.visualMetaphor: Show exploring from the root down branches; one level or one branch at a time.

content.body: Now look at the subtree rooted at 2 (originally left child). It has left child 1 and right child 3. After swapping at node 2, what are its new left and right children?
content.title: Go deeper
content.visualMetaphor: Show exploring from the root down branches; one level or one branch at a time.

content.body: Consider the subtree rooted at 7 (originally right child). It has left child 6 and right child 9. After swapping at node 7, what happens? Notice we're exploring one branch at a time from the root downward.
content.title: One more level
content.visualMetaphor: Show exploring from the root down branches; one level or one branch at a time.

content.body: You manually swapped children at each node, working your way down the tree. This is like exploring branches from the root—you visited nodes level by level or branch by branch.
content.title: What you did

content.body: Doing this manually for a large tree with hundreds of nodes would be tedious and error-prone. We need a systematic way to visit every node and swap its children. Can't figure out how to automate it? The next step will show you.
content.title: Why it gets hard

content.body: Trees are explored by starting at the root and moving down branches. We can visit nodes in a specific order (like depth-first), and at each node, we swap its left and right children. The base case is when we reach an empty tree (null)—we stop there.
content.title: Key idea
content.visualMetaphor: Use branch/root visual reasoning; visiting nodes or exploring levels one at a time.

content.body: We'll use recursion: at each node, swap its left and right children, then recursively invert the left subtree and the right subtree. The recursion naturally explores branches from the root downward. Empty tree (null) is our base case—we return null.
content.title: The approach
content.visualMetaphor: Show exploring from the root down branches; one level or one branch at a time.

content.body:
1. If the current node is null, return null (base case).
2. Swap the left and right children of the current node.
3. Recursively invert the left subtree.
4. Recursively invert the right subtree.
5. Return the node (now with swapped children and inverted subtrees).
content.title: Steps

steps.title: Define the function
steps.instruction: Create a function called invertTree that takes one parameter root (the root node of a binary tree). Start with the base case: if root is null, return null.
steps.hint: Remember, an empty tree is represented by null.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function should handle empty trees correctly.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you return null explicitly.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's start simple: check if root is null and return null in that case.

steps.title: Swap children
steps.instruction: Now, swap the left and right children of the current node. Use a temporary variable to hold one side during the swap.
steps.hint: You can assign root.left to a temp, then swap.
steps.expectedOutcome: The left and right pointers should be exchanged.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Almost there. Make sure you're swapping, not just assigning one side.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try using a temporary variable: let temp = root.left; then assign root.left = root.right; and root.right = temp;

steps.title: Recurse on subtrees
steps.instruction: Finally, recursively invert the left and right subtrees. Call invertTree on root.left and root.right (after swapping). Return the root at the end.
steps.hint: The recursion will explore branches from the current node downward.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function should invert the entire tree by visiting every node.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Close! Don't forget to call invertTree on both subtrees.

content.body: You've successfully inverted a binary tree! Remember: trees are explored from the root down branches, recursion naturally follows this pattern, and the base case (empty tree) stops the recursion. This approach visits every node exactly once, making it efficient.
content.title: Done
